turns.content: i need to tell someone this. i've been hiding a credit card from my wife for 18 months. she doesn't know about the debt. it's around 14k.

That's a heavy thing to carry around for 18 months. Thanks for telling someone.

Can I ask - what's been stopping you from telling her?
i mean it's not really lying. she never asked. and i pay it from my own account.

I hear you, but I think you know that's a bit of a stretch. Hiding $14k in debt from your spouse is pretty much the definition of a financial secret, even if she never directly asked.

What would you think if the situation were reversed and she had done the same thing?
am i a bad person. just say it.

No, you're not a bad person. But you're doing something that could seriously hurt your marriage if it comes out on its own terms.

Good people hide things when they're scared or ashamed. That doesn't make the hiding okay though.

What are you actually afraid will happen if you tell her?
ok the real reason i can't tell her is because she'll think i'm the same as her ex who hid money from her. and i'm not. i'm not that kind of person.

That context changes everything. No wonder you've been paralyzed about this.

But here's the hard truth - right now you ARE doing the same thing he did, even if your intentions and character are completely different. And the longer it stays hidden, the more it looks like his behavior, not less.

Telling her yourself, proactively, is actually the thing that proves you're different from him. His kind of person doesn't come clean voluntarily.

Does she know that's a sensitive area for you too?
what do i do. just tell me what to do.

Tell her. Soon. Like this week.

Pick a calm moment, no distractions, and lead with the most important part first - that you've been hiding something and you're ashamed, and you need her to hear you out.

Something like: *"I need to tell you something I should have told you a long time ago. I have a credit card you don't know about with $14k on it. I hid it because I was scared, not because I was trying to deceive you. I know how that sounds given your history and I'm so sorry."*

Then let her react. Don't over-explain or defend yourself right away. Just let her feel what she feels.

The conversation will be brutal. But you finding out she discovered it on her own would be so much worse. That's the moment you actually become her ex in her eyes.

You ready to do this?
